briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek R2 escalate multi-agent race with new coordination benchmarks

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI frontier continues rapid expansion with new model releases from major labs driving competitive tension. Funding remains robust across infrastructure and applications. Regulatory focus sharpens on security vulnerabilities amid accelerating deployment.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with advanced multi-agent orchestration while Anthropic's Claude 4.5 improved reasoning depth. Google DeepMind and Meta advanced open-weight alternatives, with xAI and DeepSeek pushing inference efficiency gains.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target agentic systems while major labs report ongoing red-teaming efforts.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC and Samsung ramp 3nm AI chip production as Microsoft and Google announce new data center clusters in Europe and Asia. Energy constraints prompt renewed focus on nuclear co-location for training clusters.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent protocol standardization emerge before 2028 or will proprietary dialects fragment the ecosystem?
